text.title: Google Analytics 4 Setup Failure Modes
text.summary: Six antipatterns observed when applying Google Analytics 4 Setup. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix. Detector clauses make them mechanically catchable.

antipattern.symptom: An analyst asks for last year's cohort in BigQuery; the dataset starts in month six; the earlier period exists only in GA4's interface and is sampled or already past retention.
antipattern.root-cause: The export was treated as an optional later step; nobody knew it does not backfill.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-bigquery-export-linked-before-launch`: link the export and set 14-month retention as part of property creation; record the link date in the config.

antipattern.symptom: Events carry `plan_tier` for months; the report builder cannot find it; after registration the dimension shows `(not set)` for every earlier date.

root-cause.source: Google Analytics Help, 'Custom dimensions and metrics'

antipattern.root-cause: Parameters were added in code without registering the dimension; registration was assumed retroactive.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-custom-dimensions-registered-within-limits`: registration is a step in the same change as the code, scoped correctly, with the used-slot count tracked against the plan limit.

antipattern.symptom: Page views are roughly double the sessions' screen count; engagement rate per page halves; the SPA router pushes `page_view` while enhanced measurement also fires on history change.
antipattern.root-cause: Enhanced measurement's history-change page view was left on while the app sent its own.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-enhanced-measurement-declared-no-double-page-view`: declare every toggle in the config; pick manual `page_view` with `send_page_view: false` or the automatic option, never both.

antipattern.symptom: The top converting source is `paypal.com / referral` or the SSO domain; paid campaigns show near-zero purchases; session count per buyer is two.
antipattern.root-cause: The unwanted-referral list was empty; the return from the payment page started a new attributed session.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-internal-traffic-referral-and-cross-domain`: list every payment and auth domain as an unwanted referral; add cross-domain measurement when checkout lives on another domain.

antipattern.symptom: The consent banner is present, yet `_ga` cookies exist before it is answered; Google Ads flags EEA conversions as unmeasurable; the CMP logs show the default push arriving after the first hit.
antipattern.root-cause: The `gtag('consent','default')` call was placed after `gtag('config')` or omitted; `ad_user_data` and `ad_personalization` were not included.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-consent-mode-v2-defaults-before-config`: defaults with all four signals precede the config call in the snippet; QA verifies no vendor cookie before consent.

antipattern.symptom: After a Measurement Protocol integration, new users double, sessions per user drop to one, and every server-side purchase attributes to `(direct)`.
antipattern.root-cause: The server generated a UUID instead of reading the `_ga` cookie; `session_id` was omitted.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-measurement-protocol-reuses-client-id`: pass the browser's `client_id` and `session_id` on every hit, and keep the `api_secret` server-side.

section.title: Human checkpoint
section.p: Before any binding action driven by a Google Analytics 4 Setup output (creating or relinking a property, changing retention, marking key events, changing consent defaults), a named human reviewer must sign off. The agent surfaces a `ready_for_review=true` flag and does NOT auto-commit decisions, copy, configs, or rollouts.
